The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Design Review Committee
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular Meetings are held on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of every month.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a modification
or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Clerk’s Office at (626) 300-0705
at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij, Howard Brody, Kevin Cheng, Christa Lakon, Peter Wong,
  Alternate Committee Member Ben Lundgren

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall, 2200 Huntington
Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive and the Recreation Department, 1560 Pasqualito
Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s Website: http://www.cityofsanmarino.org

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the Design
Review Committee on any item of interest to the public, before or during the Design Review Committee’s
consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Design Review Committee.

OPEN FORUM

This is an opportunity for future applicants to informally present preliminary design concepts for feedback from
members of the DRC. Comments received are based on members not having visited the site and neighborhood.
Therefore, positive comments should not be perceived as preliminary approval of a project but rather as a tool
in facilitating a project through the Design Review process. No more than two DRC members may participate
in Open Forum discussions. Applications that have been heard by the DRC may not be discussed during Open
Forum.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA – JULY 3, 2019  PAGE 3 OF 3

PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED

All public writings distributed by the City of San Marino to at least a majority of the Design Review Committee
regarding any item on this agenda will be made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200
Huntington Drive, San Marino, California.

ADJOURNMENT

The San Marino Design Review Committee will adjourn to the next regular meeting to be held on Wednesday,
July 17, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 2200 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California.

APPEALS

There is a fifteen day appeal period for all applications. All appeals should be filed with the Planning and Building
Department. Please contact the Planning and Building Department for further information.

TO:  Chair and Members of the Design Review Committee

FROM:  Eva Choi, Associate Planner
DATE:  July 3, 2019
SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC19-11
  2375 MELVILLE DR., (CHENG)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a one-story addition to an existing single-story residence.

TREE PRESERVATION

This project will not result in tree removal, it is not near any matured trees or tree canopies.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

June 19, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC. The project was not heard due to lack of a
quorum.
July 3, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC.
August 4, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 9
Object – 0
No response – 3
 DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application
if it finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed single-story addition in the rear of the structure maintains the
  existing facade. The increased massing and building volume are in keeping with
  development pattern in the legal neighborhood.

  2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner
  which balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on
  contiguous properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to
  develop their property within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The addition provides two new windows along the west side yard that is in
  close proximity to the west neighbor’s garage structure, these new windows will not
  provide a direct sightline into the neighbor’s structure. Staff does not anticipate any
  privacy issues associated with this project.

  3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing
  building which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The project integrates with the existing structure seamlessly; it provides
  consistent roof slope and maintains the existing architectural style. The project
  enhances the building articulation along the north elevation.

  4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building
  or structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The project provides consistent façade treatments including window and
  roofing materials, matching color and finished materials are carried throughout the
  entire structure. Exterior lighting fixtures are equipped with seeded glass to reduce
  lighting pollution. The new family room consists of two sets of aluminum MultiGlideTM
  door from the Anderson Architectural Collection. The design and operation of the
  gliding doors complement an indoor-outdoor living lifestyle. The applicant has submitted
  a product brochure for your consideration.

  Howard Brody

SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC18-73
  605 CHESTER AVE., (TAM)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a one-story addition to an existing single-story residence,
construct exterior modifications to the existing detached garage and construct a street-facing
side yard wall.

TREE PRESERVATION

This project requires tree pruning along the west property line to accommodate the paving for
the new driveway. There is a mature jacaranda tree near the addition. Staff recommends that
fencing and a tree protection plan be provided to prevent damage to the jacaranda tree during
construction. Staff recommends that the project be conditioned to submit a tree protection
plan for approval by the City Arborist.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

June 19, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC. The Committee continued the hearing citing
concerns with an oak tree adjacent to the garage and the driveway approach.
July 3, 2019 – Second hearing before the DRC
August 4, 2019 – Required action date
 NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 13
Object – 0
No response – 1

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS - ADDITION

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application
if it finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed location and massing of the addition is compatible with the
  neighborhood. The structure maintains its existing appearance as viewed from the
  streets. The relocation of the garage door to face California Boulevard is consistent
  with three other street-facing garages along the same side of California Boulevard
  between Sierra Madre Boulevard and San Marino Avenue.

  2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner
  which balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on
  contiguous properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to
  develop their property within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: A new window is introduced along the south side yard and this window will
  not provide a direct sightline into the neighbor’s structure. Staff does not anticipate any
  privacy issues associated with this project.

  3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing
  building which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The addition is compatible with the existing rooflines and utilizes consistent
  design details.

  4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building
  or structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  2
   Comments: The proposed colors and materials are consistently carried throughout the
  structure. The existing tile roof material is a custom blended color, the architect stated
  that the project will provide matching tiles. The existing driveway gate operation will
  need to be modified from sliding open in front of the garage to a swing gate that opens
  toward the residence to accommodate access through the new garage door. The
  project provides decorative paving along the new driveway, staff recommends that
  paving material color be similar to natural washed concrete and that the paving should
  not extend to the property line in order to minimize the appearance of the expanded
  paving area.

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS - SIDE YARD WALL ADJACNET TO A STREET

San Marino City Code Section 23.13.04G identifies separate design review findings relating to
the approval of fence, gates, walls and pilasters. The Design Review Committee may not
reduce the maximum permitted height, increase the minimum required setback or decrease the
maximum permitted opacity of any fence, gate, yard wall or retaining wall located in a side yard
adjacent to a street; except, that the Design Review Committee can increase the minimum
setback for a gate providing access to a driveway in order to protect pedestrian or vehicular
traffic.

The DRC shall approve the application for the side yard wall adjacent to a street if it finds all of
the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall is
  architecturally compatible with the existing residence.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed side yard block wall will have a stucco finish with matching
  color as the residence. Staff recommends that the proposed decorative pedestrian gates
  be made of wrought iron material, in a design and color matching the existing driveway
  gate.

  2. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall is
  consistent with the size and location of fences, gates, pilasters, yard walls and
  retaining walls on the block on which the property is located.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  The Municipal Code defines Block as the property abutting on one side of a street and
  lying between the two (2) nearest intersecting or intercepting streets or between the
  termination of such street and the nearest intersecting or intercepting street.

  Comments: For the purpose of analyzing compatibility with existing residences, Staff
  observed that the west neighbor at 610 San Marino Avenue is developed with a similar
  block wall running along California Boulevard.

  3
 3. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall preserves
  site lines and is otherwise located in a manner not to create a hazard to
  pedestrian or vehicular traffic.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed side yard block wall will not create a traffic hazard. The block
  wall will serve to close off the side yard in addition to the existing hedge, it will not
  impact visual clearance from the driveway.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a first and second story addition to an existing two-story
residence.

TREE PRESERVATION

There are no proposed tree removals as part of this project. There is one mature oak tree and
one mature sycamore tree. An arborist’s report has been provided as part of this application,
but staff also recommends a condition of approval requiring a tree protection plan to be
submitted prior to the issuance of a building permit to demonstrate the continued safety of the
existing trees during any construction.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

July 3, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
August 4, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 8
Object – 0
No response – 2
 DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application
if it finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments:  The legal neighborhood is comprised of predominantly two-story
  structures in various architectural styles. Although the proposed addition is located
  behind the house, it would still be visible from public view and adds massing to the
  south elevation, resulting in a disruption to the rhythm of the overall design of the
  Colonial style of the house. The neighborhood consists of mostly traditional
  architectural styles, so in order to maintain compatibility, the subject property should
  retain the symmetrical façade that is expected of a Colonial style house.

  2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner which
  balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on contiguous
  properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to develop their property
  within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: Two new windows are proposed along the south and north elevations. Staff
  finds that these windows do not compromise the reasonable expectation of privacy for
  the adjacent neighbor since there is a sufficient setback distance between the proposed
  addition and the neighbors’ structures. Visibility into adjacent structures does not
  appear to be a prominent issue.

  3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing building
  which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐ YES  ☒ NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comment: Staff finds that the proposed addition is not a well-integrated extension of
  the existing building. Staff acknowledges that there are physical constraints on the
  property with respect to the two mature trees in the rear yard. However, the project
  can be designed in a manner that would maintain the integrity of the architectural style
  of the building without looking like an obvious add-on. Staff is not able to make this
  finding as there is an alternative option available to reduce the size of the addition and
  reconfigure the floor plan accordingly.

  4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or
  structure.

  2
 Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

Comments: All colors and materials are proposed to match those that are existing on
the structure. The proposed windows and doors are selected from the City’s Pre-
Approved list.

  I was contacted by Paul Wang regarding two trees located in his back yard one being a Sycamore
and the other a live Oak. Paul is currently in the beginning stages of planning for a room addition and
balcony and was asked by the city to provide an arborist report to help minimize the impact of the
construction near the trees and to see how far they can encroach on the trees with out impacting the
health or destabilizing them.

  Tree # 1 a Coastal live Oak (Quercus agrifolia) has a dbh of 28 inches, its height is approximately
40 feet tall and the spread is approximately 40 feet as well. The tree appears to be healthy, it has a full
canopy, and plenty of space for the roots to thrive, there are no signs of fruiting bodies indicating any
type of root disease. The tree is approximately 15 feet away from the proposed construction site and
the location of either the foundation and or pillars are just outside the dripline of the tree. The
customer is willing to use a pillar type foundation in order to minimize the impact to the trees root
system and to prevent damage to a traditional type foundation in the future, this would be the best
solution to minimize impact on the tree and to prevent future maintenance issues in the future.

  Tree #2 a Western Sycamore (Platanus racemosa) is a multi-trunk tree with a combined dbh of
53 inches, a height of approximately 50 feet, and a spread of approximately 50 feet. The tree appears
healthy with no structural defects aside from a very heavy lean. The customer is proposing the same
thing be done as far as the construction of the pillars and or foundation, to minimize impact to the tree,
the trees dripline does not extend into the area of construction posing no problem to the tree,
   Attached is a general tree protection plan which should be adhered to at all times, this is to
maintain the health of the tree.

  I would say that if all guidelines are adhered to there should be no risk to either of the trees
moving forward with the project.

  Thank you for your time and consideration on this matter please feel free to contact me with
any questions or concerns.

  Jeffery Carlton
